data.title: Aminoglycosides: gentamicin (systemic + topical) & amikacin
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Other antibacterials_

**Class:** Aminoglycoside antibiotics

## Mechanism of action
- Bind 30S ribosomal subunit → mRNA misreading → bactericidal (concentration-dependent; oxygen-dependent uptake, so inactive against anaerobes)
- Amikacin is resistant to most aminoglycoside-inactivating enzymes — the most broad-spectrum

## Pharmacokinetics
- Not absorbed orally; IV/IM; renal excretion — dose by renal function; once-daily dosing exploits post-antibiotic effect

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Gentamicin IV/IM: serious Gram-negative infections (Pseudomonas), with β-lactams in endocarditis; donovanosis (adjunct); plague, tularaemia
- Gentamicin topical 0.1% cream/ointment: impetigo, infected wounds, Pseudomonas-infected toe webs/nails (resistance and sensitisation limit use)
- Amikacin: actinomycetoma (Welsh regimen — amikacin 15 mg/kg/day in cycles with co-trimoxazole), rapid-growing NTM, MDR-TB (older regimens), Nocardia

## Dose & formulations
- Gentamicin 5–7 mg/kg IV once daily (adjust to levels)
- Amikacin 15 mg/kg/day (e.g. 500 mg twice daily) IM/IV; Welsh regimen: 3-week cycles with 2-week gaps, up to 3–4 cycles, with co-trimoxazole
- Topical gentamicin 3–4 times daily, short courses

## Adverse effects
- Nephrotoxicity (acute tubular necrosis, reversible)
- Ototoxicity — cochlear (amikacin) and vestibular (gentamicin, streptomycin); often irreversible; mitochondrial gene variant increases risk
- Neuromuscular blockade (avoid in myasthenia)
- Topical: contact allergy (cross-reacts with neomycin/framycetin)

## Contraindications
- Pregnancy (fetal ototoxicity); myasthenia gravis; pre-existing hearing loss
- Topical on large raw areas or perforated tympanic membrane

## Drug interactions
- Loop diuretics, vancomycin, amphotericin B, cisplatin, cyclosporine: additive oto/nephrotoxicity
- Neuromuscular blockers potentiated

## Monitoring
- Renal function, trough levels, audiometry (baseline and during long amikacin courses — mycetoma)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid (old FDA category D).

## Viva points
- Welsh regimen for actinomycetoma — amikacin + co-trimoxazole
- Ototoxicity: amikacin cochlear, gentamicin/streptomycin vestibular
- Topical gentamicin sensitises and cross-reacts with neomycin

_Sources: Khopkar ch.1 (Aminoglycosides, Amikacin) and ch.18 (topical gentamicin); Wolverton 4e ch.9 and ch.41. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
